title: Manage application settings with Azure App Configuration

questions.q: An app's managed identity only needs to read settings and feature flags from App Configuration. Which role should it get?

options.text: Key Vault Secrets User on a vault
options.why: That's for Key Vault secrets.

options.text: App Configuration Data Owner
options.why: Data Owner is for operators and pipelines that change settings.

options.text: App Configuration Data Reader
options.why: Correct. Read-only access to key-values, feature flags and Key Vault references.

options.text: Contributor on the resource group
options.why: Contributor manages the resource, not least-privilege data reads.

questions.hint: Reading settings and flags only: the read-only data role.
questions.explain: Readers for apps, Owners for operators.

questions.q: What is the endpoint format for an App Configuration store named docpipe-config?

options.text: https://docpipe-config.azconfig.io
options.why: Correct. Stores use https://<store-name>.azconfig.io.

options.text: https://docpipe-config.config.azure.com
options.why: That isn't the App Configuration domain.

options.text: https://docpipe-config.vault.azure.net
options.why: That's a Key Vault URL.

options.text: https://docpipe-config.azurewebsites.net
options.why: That's App Service.

questions.hint: App Configuration endpoints use their own domain.
questions.explain: Pass the endpoint and a credential to load().

questions.q: For each statement, select Yes if the statement is true. Otherwise, select No. An app calls `load(endpoint=…, credential=DefaultAzureCredential())` with no selectors.

rows.text: It loads keys labelled Production as well as unlabelled keys.
rows.why: Without a selector, only null-label keys load.

rows.text: Keys are case-insensitive, so openai:endpoint matches OpenAI:Endpoint.
A key plus its value can be up to 10 KB.
The returned object can be used like a Python dictionary.

questions.hint: No selector means null-label keys only. Keys are case-sensitive. There's a size limit.
questions.explain: Use SettingSelector to choose keys and labels.

questions.q: Several apps share one store, and this app's keys all start with DocPipeline:. The code should use short names like OpenAI:Endpoint. What should you use?

options.text: A separate App Configuration store for each key
options.why: A store per key isn't how prefixes are handled.

options.text: A label_filter set to the value DocPipeline
options.why: Labels are variants, not key prefixes.

options.text: Tags named DocPipeline on every one of the keys
options.why: Tags don't shorten key names.

options.text: key_filter DocPipeline:* plus trim_prefixes
options.why: Correct. Filter by prefix, then trim it for cleaner names.

questions.hint: Filter on the app's prefix, then remove it from the names the code sees.
questions.explain: key_filter narrows what loads; trim_prefixes simplifies names.

questions.q: An operator updates three model settings and wants running apps to pick up all three together, not one at a time. What's the pattern?

options.text: Add a label called Refresh to the three keys
options.why: Labels don't trigger refresh.

options.text: Set refresh_interval to 0 so every key refreshes instantly
options.why: The provider still needs refresh() calls and a watched key; per-key instant refresh isn't the pattern.

options.text: Restart each app instance after every single change
options.why: Restarts aren't needed with dynamic refresh.

options.text: Change the settings, then the Sentinel key
options.why: Correct. A sentinel change triggers a reload of the whole configuration for consistency.

questions.hint: Change the settings, then touch one key that tells apps to reload.
questions.explain: Sentinel key + refresh_on + refresh(): changes take effect together.

questions.q: Dynamic refresh is configured with refresh_interval=60, but the app never sees updated values. The code only calls load() at startup. What's missing?

options.text: Calls to config.refresh() in the app
options.why: Correct. The provider's refresh() must be called explicitly.

options.text: The App Configuration Data Owner role
options.why: Reading doesn't need Data Owner.

options.text: A second load() call every 60 seconds
options.why: Reloading by hand isn't the provider's refresh mechanism.

options.text: A label_filter set to the null label
options.why: Labels aren't the issue.

questions.hint: Refresh doesn't happen by itself. The app must ask for it.
questions.explain: refresh() checks the watch keys if the interval has elapsed; otherwise it returns immediately.

questions.q: A setting Pipeline:Stages holds a JSON array, but the app receives it as a plain string and has to parse it by hand. What should you set on the key-value?

options.text: Content type application/json
options.why: Correct. The provider then parses the value as a JSON object.

options.text: A key name ending in .json
options.why: The key's name doesn't tell the provider how to parse the value.

options.text: A label named json
options.why: Labels create variants of a key. They don't change how the value is parsed.

options.text: A tag type=json
options.why: Tags are metadata for filtering. They don't affect parsing.

questions.hint: One optional property tells the provider how to interpret the value.
questions.explain: Each setting has a key, value, optional label, optional content type and tags. Setting content type to application/json tells the provider to parse the value as a JSON object.

questions.q: An app connects to App Configuration with a connection string stored in an environment variable. Security wants no connection strings at all. What should the app use?

options.text: Its managed identity with the App Configuration Data Reader role
options.why: Correct. A managed identity removes the connection string and its rotation burden.

options.text: The store's access key in local.settings.json
options.why: That's another shared secret, not an identity.

options.text: Anonymous access with an IP allow list
options.why: App Configuration isn't meant for anonymous access, and IPs aren't identities.

options.text: A connection string stored in Key Vault instead
options.why: That still uses a connection string that grants full access to the store.

questions.hint: Remove the secret entirely by authenticating as the app itself.
questions.explain: Managed identities remove connection strings from configuration. The app identity needs App Configuration Data Reader to read key-values, feature flags and Key Vault references.

questions.q: A new document classification stage starts producing wrong labels in production. What lets operators turn it off in seconds without redeploying?

options.text: A new label on the Pipeline:BatchSize key
options.why: Labels vary values per environment, not stage on/off.

options.text: A feature flag used as a kill switch
options.why: Correct. Disable the flag and the pipeline skips the stage.

options.text: A Key Vault reference for the stage
options.why: Key Vault references point to secrets.

options.text: A code rollback through the pipeline
options.why: Rollbacks take minutes or hours.

questions.hint: Turning something off in seconds without a deployment is a flag's job.
questions.explain: Feature flags decouple feature lifecycle from deployment.

questions.q: Defaults are stored with no label and production overrides with the Production label. In which order should the SettingSelectors be passed?

options.text: Production alone, with no defaults
options.why: Keys without overrides would be missing.

options.text: Production first, then null label
options.why: Defaults would then override production values.

options.text: Null label first, then Production
options.why: Correct. Later selectors override earlier ones, so overrides go last.

options.text: The null label alone, with a Production tag
options.why: Tags don't select labels.

questions.hint: Later selectors override earlier ones, so defaults go first.
questions.explain: Stack defaults, then environment-specific overrides.

questions.q: For each statement, select Yes if the statement is true. Otherwise, select No. An app loads settings with `feature_flag_enabled=True` and `feature_flag_refresh_enabled=True`.

rows.text: Changing a feature flag also triggers a refresh of regular settings.
FeatureManager comes with the provider package, with no extra install.
is_enabled("UseNewEmbeddingsModel") returns a boolean for the flag's state.

questions.hint: Flag refresh and setting refresh are separate. FeatureManager is a separate package.
questions.explain: Flags and settings refresh independently when refresh() is called.

questions.q: How does App Configuration store feature flags internally?

options.text: In a separate store that FeatureManager alone reads
options.why: Flags live in the same store.

options.text: Keys prefixed .appconfig.featureflag/
options.why: Correct. The libraries hide these details behind simple flag names.

options.text: As labels named Enabled and Disabled on keys
options.why: Labels are environment variants, not flag states.

options.text: As Key Vault secrets with a FeatureFlag tag
options.why: Flags aren't Key Vault secrets.

questions.hint: Feature flags are stored as ordinary key-values under a reserved prefix.
questions.explain: Prefix .appconfig.featureflag/ with content type application/vnd.microsoft.appconfig.ff+json.

questions.q: Which two scenarios does Learn list as feature flag patterns for AI apps? (Select two.)

options.text: Progressive rollout of a new embeddings model
options.why: Correct. Gate the new model's code path before full rollout.

options.text: Rotating a Cosmos DB connection string
options.why: Rotation is a Key Vault concern.

options.text: Storing the Azure OpenAI API key
options.why: Secrets belong in Key Vault.

options.text: Staged activation of pipeline stages
options.why: Correct. Enable stages one at a time.

questions.hint: Learn lists a set of flag patterns for AI apps. Two of these match it.
questions.explain: Rollouts, kill switches, A/B tests and staged activation.

questions.q: The team wants to compare the current embedding configuration with an experimental one on live requests, sending some requests down each path. Which feature flag pattern from Learn fits?

options.text: A sentinel key
options.why: The sentinel key triggers a configuration refresh. It isn't a feature flag pattern.

options.text: A/B testing configurations
options.why: Correct. Flags can route different requests through different paths so that you can compare results.

options.text: A kill switch
options.why: A kill switch turns a stage off in an emergency. It doesn't compare two paths.

options.text: Staged pipeline activation
options.why: Staged activation turns stages on one at a time. It doesn't compare configurations.

questions.hint: Two paths running side by side so that you can compare their results.
questions.explain: Learn's feature flag patterns for AI apps: progressive model rollouts, kill switches, A/B testing configurations, and staged pipeline activation.

questions.q: OpenAI:ApiKey is a Key Vault reference. Loading fails with an error naming the vault and secret, although other settings load fine. What's most likely missing?

options.text: Key Vault Secrets User on that vault
options.why: Correct. Store access works, but resolving the reference needs vault access.

options.text: A label on the OpenAI:ApiKey key itself
options.why: Labels don't affect resolution permissions.

options.text: App Configuration Data Owner on the store
options.why: Reading settings needs Data Reader, which already works.

options.text: The featuremanagement package installed
options.why: Feature management is unrelated.

questions.hint: The reference resolves in Key Vault, so the identity needs a secrets role there too.
questions.explain: The identity needs a role on App Configuration and on every referenced vault.

questions.q: You create a reference with `--secret-identifier https://my-keyvault.vault.azure.net/secrets/openai-api-key` (no version). What happens when the secret rotates?

options.text: App Configuration copies the new value into the store
options.why: App Configuration stores only the pointer.

options.text: Nothing; versionless identifiers are pinned to the first version
options.why: Versionless means latest, not first.

options.text: The reference breaks until you update it
options.why: Versionless references keep working after rotation.

options.text: The app gets the new value on its next load or secret refresh
options.why: Correct. Omitting the version resolves the latest version.

questions.hint: A versionless reference follows rotation.
questions.explain: Omit the version so rotated secrets are picked up automatically.

questions.q: For each statement, select Yes if the statement is true. Otherwise, select No. An app loads settings with `keyvault_credential=DefaultAzureCredential()` and `secret_refresh_interval=3600`.

rows.text: App Configuration stores the actual secret value for OpenAI:ApiKey.
rows.why: It stores only the reference URI.

rows.text: Application code needs a separate SecretClient to read OpenAI:ApiKey.
Secrets can be re-resolved hourly while settings are checked more often.
Secret refresh happens only when the app calls refresh().
rows.why: The refresh call triggers re-resolution once the interval elapses.

questions.hint: App Configuration stores a pointer. The provider resolves it.
questions.explain: One load() returns settings and resolved secrets; each has its own refresh cadence.

questions.q: Production and Development must use different OpenAI API keys stored in different vaults, under the same key name OpenAI:ApiKey. How?

options.text: Two keys named OpenAI:ApiKey:Prod and OpenAI:ApiKey:Dev in code
options.why: Environment-specific key names are what labels avoid.

options.text: Store both secret values directly in App Configuration
options.why: Secrets shouldn't be stored directly in App Configuration.

options.text: Two labelled references for OpenAI:ApiKey
options.why: Correct. Labels work on references just like other keys.

options.text: Use tags to choose the vault at runtime
options.why: Tags don't select values at load time.

questions.hint: Labels work for references too.
questions.explain: Label references to point to environment-specific vaults.

questions.q: A configuration has 80 Key Vault references and secret_refresh_interval of 10 seconds across 30 instances. What should you consider?

options.text: Total Key Vault requests against its limits
options.why: Correct. Each resolution is a Key Vault request; choose an interval that fits limits and rotation.

options.text: Nothing; references are cached by App Configuration
options.why: Each resolution generates a request to Key Vault.

options.text: App Configuration's 10 KB value limit
options.why: The pointer is small; the issue is request volume.

options.text: Moving the references into feature flags
options.why: Feature flags aren't for secrets.

questions.hint: Many references, frequent refresh and many instances multiply into Key Vault calls.
questions.explain: Align secret refresh with your rotation schedule and Key Vault limits.

questions.q: A Key Vault reference was created with --secret-identifier that ends in a version ID. The secret rotates monthly, but the app keeps loading the old value. Why?

options.text: App Configuration caches secret values for 30 days
options.why: App Configuration stores only the pointer, not the secret value.

options.text: The app's identity lacks App Configuration Data Owner
options.why: Reading references needs Data Reader. A missing role would fail, not return old values.

options.text: The reference is pinned to that secret version
options.why: Correct. Including a version in the URI pins the reference; leave it out to follow rotation.

options.text: Key Vault references refresh only when the store is restarted
options.why: Stores aren't restarted, and the provider re-resolves versionless references.

questions.hint: Look at the end of the secret URI.
questions.explain: --secret-identifier accepts the full URI; appending a version pins the reference to that version. Use a versionless URI so the app gets the new value on its next load or secret refresh.

questions.q: Settings load, but every Key Vault reference fails to resolve. The app identity has App Configuration Data Reader on the store. What else does it need?

options.text: Key Vault Secrets User on the referenced vault
options.why: Correct. References resolve in Key Vault, so the identity needs permissions on both services.

options.text: Key Vault Contributor on the vault
options.why: Contributor is control-plane only, so it can't read secret values.

options.text: Nothing, because App Configuration reads the secret for the app
options.why: App Configuration stores only the pointer. The app's identity reads the secret.

options.text: App Configuration Data Owner on the store
options.why: Data Owner adds write access to the store. It doesn't grant access to the vault.

questions.hint: The secret lives in a different service from the setting.
questions.explain: For Key Vault references to resolve, the application identity needs permissions on both App Configuration (Data Reader) and Key Vault (Key Vault Secrets User).

questions.q: Match each setting to where Learn says it belongs.
questions.hint: Ask whether the value grants access or only changes behavior.
questions.explain: If the value alone grants access, it belongs in Key Vault.

questions.q: For each statement, select Yes if the statement is true. Otherwise, select No. A team reviews its configuration design.

rows.text: Storing the Azure OpenAI API key directly as an App Configuration value is fine because the store is encrypted.
rows.why: Secrets miss Key Vault's per-access audit, rotation and HSM protection.

rows.text: Putting batch sizes in Key Vault is a good way to secure them.
rows.why: Non-sensitive values in Key Vault waste its capabilities and risk throttling.

rows.text: Keeping a copy of a connection string in both services without a reference can cause drift.
rows.why: Use a reference so there's one source of truth.

questions.hint: Credentials belong in Key Vault, behavior in App Configuration.
questions.explain: Each service for its intended purpose, linked by references.

questions.q: Which App Configuration capability lets operators roll back the whole configuration to a known point in time?

options.text: Key-value snapshots
options.why: Correct. Snapshots support point-in-time rollback.

options.text: Purge protection
options.why: Purge protection is a Key Vault feature.

options.text: Secret versioning
options.why: Secret versioning is Key Vault's.

options.text: Event Grid subscriptions
options.why: Event Grid delivers events; it doesn't roll back config.

questions.hint: One App Configuration feature captures a whole configuration at a point in time.
questions.explain: App Configuration: labels, flags, snapshots, dynamic refresh.

questions.q: Compliance requires a record of which identity read each credential and when. Why does this push the credential into Key Vault?

options.text: App Configuration can't store strings longer than 1 KB
options.why: The limit is 10 KB for key + value, and size isn't the reason.

options.text: Key Vault tracks each access; App Config RBAC is store-level
options.why: Correct. Per-object access tracking needs Key Vault.

options.text: Key Vault values refresh faster than App Configuration
options.why: Refresh speed isn't the criterion.

options.text: App Configuration doesn't support managed identities
options.why: App Configuration supports managed identity.

questions.hint: Key Vault logs every access to each secret.
questions.explain: Per-access audit, rotation and expiry are Key Vault strengths.

questions.q: Which value belongs in Key Vault rather than App Configuration, according to Learn's placement rule?

options.text: The model deployment name text-embedding-ada-002
options.why: A deployment name controls behavior without granting access.

options.text: A database connection string that contains a password
options.why: Correct. Values that grant access or contain credentials are sensitive and belong in Key Vault.

options.text: The Azure OpenAI endpoint URL
options.why: An endpoint URL alone doesn't grant access, so it's an App Configuration value.

options.text: The pipeline's retry count
options.why: Retry counts control behavior, so they belong in App Configuration.

questions.hint: The test is whether the value grants access to a resource.
questions.explain: The key criterion is whether a value grants access or contains credentials. Endpoints, deployment names, dimensions, batch sizes and flags go to App Configuration; API keys and connection strings with credentials go to Key Vault.
